styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old Dhaka lanes, rickshaw art and river life.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Biryani, kebabs and street sweets all day.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Mughal forts, mosques and the 1971 story.

stays.why: Quiet, green and full of good restaurants and cafés. Easy for ride apps and the airport road.
Next to Gulshan, with malls, bakeries and many mid-range hotels. Calmer than the old city.
The business heart and a stop on the MRT Line 6 metro. Good value and central for the new city.
Steps from Lalbagh Fort, Ahsan Manzil and the food streets. Lively and loud; basic rooms for less.

food: Start with kacchi biryani, Dhaka's signature rice dish. Old Dhaka spots are famous; go early for lunch.
Try kebabs and borhani, a salty yogurt drink that cools the spice. Cheap and filling.
Street sweets: roshogolla, sandesh and mishti doi. Buy from busy shops with high turnover.
Old Dhaka food walks along Nazira Bazar and Chawkbazar are best in the evening; go with a local guide.
Drink only bottled or filtered water. Skip ice and raw salads at street stalls if your stomach is new to the city.
more_time: Add a morning at Ahsan Manzil and the Sadarghat riverfront, then a short boat ride on the Buriganga.
Day trip to Sonargaon folk-art museum and Panam City, roughly 1–2 hours by road; check traffic before you go.
Spend an afternoon at the Liberation War Museum and the National Museum for the 1971 history.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Old Dhaka's sights and food plus the museums, with time for the river.

month_notes: January: cool and dry, highs near 24°C. The best month for walking Old Dhaka.
February: mild and dry, around 27°C. Great for sightseeing and outdoor food walks.
March: warms to 31°C with about 7 rain days. Start early; afternoons get sticky.
April: hot at 33°C and wetter, about 13 rain days. Plan indoor breaks at midday.
May: hot and humid, about 21 rain days. Carry an umbrella and expect short downpours.
June: monsoon begins, around 26 rain days. Sightseeing is possible between showers; streets flood.
July: peak monsoon, about 28 rain days. Wettest month; keep plans flexible.
August: still peak monsoon, about 28 rain days. Same advice: mornings out, afternoons indoors.
September: heavy rain continues, about 25 rain days. Slightly cooler but still wet.
October: rain eases to about 16 days. A good shoulder month as the heat drops.
November: dry and pleasant, highs near 29°C. One of the best months to visit.
December: cool and dry, around 25°C. Pack a light layer for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical monsoon climate: a cool dry winter, a hot sticky spring, and a long, very wet summer.

items.title: Best time: November to February
items.text: Dry, mild days around 24–29°C and cooler evenings. Ideal for walking and the old city.

items.title: Hot season: March to May
items.text: Highs reach 33°C with rising humidity. Go out early and rest indoors at midday.

items.title: Monsoon: June to September
items.text: Rain on 25–28 days a month. Expect flooded streets and traffic delays; carry an umbrella.

items.title: Humid most of the year
items.text: Lows stay near 24–26°C in the wet months. Light, breathable clothes help.

items.title: Pack for rain in summer
items.text: A compact umbrella and quick-dry shoes are useful from May to October.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton clothes, a hat and sunscreen; a light layer for December–January evenings; modest dress for mosques.

transit.best: The MRT Line 6 metro for cross-city trips; ride apps or CNG auto-rickshaws for the rest.

modes.text: MRT Line 6 runs Uttara to Motijheel. Cheap and fast; a good way to skip traffic.
City buses are crowded, noisy and signed only in Bengali. Hard for first-time visitors.
Uber and Pathao work in Dhaka. CNG auto-rickshaws are cheapest for longer rides; meters are rarely used, so agree the fare.
Driving yourself is not recommended; traffic is chaotic. Hire a car with a driver instead.
Often fastest for short hops; watch pollution and traffic.
Cycle rickshaws are quick for short hops. Agree the fare first.
Ferries and rocket steamers leave from Sadarghat river port.
